rulings.challenge_claim: The Song.3.5 adjuration seam is byte-solid, but strongest_rejected_alternative is a strawman: it never engages the live rival of folding Song.3.5 into the Song.3.1-3.4 seek-find unit it closes (rival-quality gap, not a boundary error).
rulings.grounds: Re-derived from bytes, and the object verifies as well as the digit. The row's quoted adjuration run collates byte at oshb:Song.3.5 and byte at oshb:Song.2.7, and the identity is in fact stronger than claimed: oshb:Song.2.7 and oshb:Song.3.5 are the same 160 codepoints with zero divergence, so whole-verse byte identity holds. Evidence tier is correct throughout (tier-1 formula anchor: the adjuration site set is 4 sites in 3 attested shapes; the Song.3.5 setumah is held at tier-3 single-witness and explicitly not the driver), so LF's own framing is right that this is a rival-quality defect and not a boundary error. The defect is real: the shipped sentence rejects a METHOD of argument (treating Song.3.5 as identical in function to Song.2.7 without separate argument) rather than a CUT, so the one structural rival that could move this boundary ships untested. It is live on the writer's own practice inside this same cluster: the Song.5.8 adjuration verse is folded INTO the narrative unit it closes WITH its rival cut disclosed, while the 2-verse refrain עַ֤ד שֶׁיָּפ֨וּחַ֙ הַיּ֔וֹם וְנָ֖סוּ הַצְּלָלִ֑ים (byte, oshb:Song.4.6; byte, oshb:Song.2.17) is folded into the wasf with no disclosure at all - three refrain-verse decisions, two opposite treatments, one disclosure. The bytes that kill the fold rival already exist and are cheap: the she-ahavah-nafshi relative formula שֶׁאָהֲבָ֖ה נַפְשִׁ֑י (byte, oshb:Song.3.4) runs Song.3.1-Song.3.4 and stops at the seam (sweep: 5 verses book-wide, skeleton tier: MT 1:7, 3:1, 3:2, 3:3, 3:4), while Song.3.5 is a whole-verse repetition of an earlier bracket. No boundary change is proposed; the span stands.
rulings.remedy: Field strongest_rejected_alternative (P01-015): replace the method-rejection with a rival-CUT rejection that names the fold - holding Song.3.5 inside the Song.3.1-Song.3.4 seek-find unit as its closing bracket - and kills it on bytes: the she-ahavah-nafshi relative formula runs Song.3.1-Song.3.4 and stops at the seam (sweep: 5 verses book-wide, skeleton tier), whereas Song.3.5 repeats the Song.2.7 bracket whole-verse (tier: byte, 160 codepoints each, zero divergence). Keep to one sentence, plus at most a second carrying the mandated rival disclosure. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS (the test that killed the original): the sentence must name a competing CUT rather than a competing argumentation method; must carry a digit-bearing sweep that names its own object; and must leave this row's isolation of a refrain verse consistent with the opposite treatment given the Song.5.8 refrain verse in the same cluster, which does disclose its rival cut.

rulings.challenge_claim: Two defects: (a) the front-seam driver hangs a 3-verse digit on a blended object, since the ascending-question formula the row itself quotes is byte-attested in 2 verses; (b) the daughters-of-Jerusalem string the row treats as belonging only elsewhere stands inside the span at MT 3:10.
rulings.grounds: Limb (a) UPHELD on re-derived bytes - the count-object test, not merely the digit. The row's own quoted run מִ֣י זֹ֗את עֹלָה֙ מִן הַמִּדְבָּ֔ר collates byte at oshb:Song.3.6 and byte at oshb:Song.8.5 but collates NONE at oshb:Song.6.10, whose question is the הַנִּשְׁקָפָ֖ה shape (byte, oshb:Song.6.10) with no ascent clause at all. Contiguous consonantal sweeps split three objects cleanly: the bare mi-zot interrogative = 3 verses (skeleton tier: MT 3:6, 6:10, 8:5); the ola-min-ha-midbar ascent clause = 2 verses (skeleton tier: MT 3:6, 8:5); the row's full quoted run = 2 verses at byte tier (MT 3:6, 8:5). The prose names the object as the mi-zot ascending-question formula and then attaches the 3-verse digit and 'two further sites later in the book' to it, so the digit's own object test fails at one of the two sites it claims. That the shared staging spine's label for this set is equally loose does not cure the row: independent re-derivation is the writer's duty and errata are expected. Limb (b) REFUTED on the bytes and on the campaign's own role-split. The row names the ADDRESS object - the daughters-of-Jerusalem vocative pair - and that object stands at MT 1:5, 2:7, 3:5, 5:8, 5:16, 8:4 (6 verses, none inside this span). The in-span string at oshb:Song.3.10 is the prefixed from-phrase מִבְּנ֖וֹת (byte, oshb:Song.3.10), which the standing role-split excludes from the address object; a substring sweep that keeps it returns 7 verses, which is the blended count and not the row's. It is interior, straddles neither of this row's seams, and is therefore not a mandated disclosure. Net corrected finding: ONE real count-object defect on the front-seam driver, not two. The rest verifies: בְּנ֥וֹת צִיּ֖וֹן (byte, oshb:Song.3.11) is the sole site (sweep: 1 verse, skeleton tier), the 2fp imperative call is attested in-verse, and the setumah marks at MT 3:5, 3:8, 3:11 are carried at tier-3 single-witness without being made drivers.
rulings.remedy: Field boundary_rationale (P01-016): re-cut the count object one of two ways - (i) keep the quoted ascent run as the named object and carry its true digit, '(sweep: 2 verses, byte tier: Song.3.6 and Song.8.5)', deleting 'two further sites'; or (ii) rename the object to the bare mi-zot interrogative, keep the 3-verse digit, label it skeleton tier, and stop attributing the quoted run to all three sites. Re-key observed_substrate_signals mi_zot.ascending_question to whichever object survives. No edit is owed for the daughters-of-Zion contrast (limb b refuted). TEST THE CURE MUST PASS (the test that killed the original): the row's own quoted run must collate at EVERY site its digit claims - oshb:Song.6.10 returns 'none' against the run as written, and any replacement digit must survive that same per-site collation.

rulings.challenge_claim: Three defects: the opener carrying the front seam is an unswept, untiered recurrence claim whose formula stands equally at MT 1:15; the byte-identical refrain interrupting the unit at MT 4:6 is never engaged; and the rival test rests on an imperative the Hebrew of MT 4:8 does not carry.
rulings.grounds: All three limbs name real defects on re-derived bytes; two need a stated correction of wording, neither of which reverses the finding. Limb 1 UPHELD: הִנָּ֨ךְ יָפָ֤ה רַעְיָתִי֙ collates byte at oshb:Song.4.1, while the same formula at oshb:Song.1.15 (הִנָּ֤ךְ יָפָה֙ רַעְיָתִ֔י) collates accent_stripped against the row's quoted run - a 2-verse formula (skeleton tier: MT 1:15, 4:1) whose other site opens no wasf, cited with no sweep digit while it carries the 3:11|4:1 seam. CORRECTION to OL's wording: the row does tier-label the quotation itself ('tier: byte'); what ships bare is the RECURRENCE claim implied by naming a formula, which campaign law requires be tier-labeled and digit-bearing at write time. Note also a live allography trap adjacent to this claim - the skeleton run for 'behold you are beautiful' collides the 2fs form at MT 1:15 and MT 4:1 with the 2ms form at MT 1:16 (3 verses at skeleton tier), so any digit here must be word-bound with the his-word-for-her anchor. Limb 2 UPHELD as a disclosure and rival-testing defect: עַ֤ד שֶׁיָּפ֨וּחַ֙ הַיּ֔וֹם וְנָ֖סוּ הַצְּלָלִ֑ים collates byte at oshb:Song.4.6 and byte at oshb:Song.2.17, a 2-verse book refrain (skeleton tier) standing between the body-part chain the row stops at web:Song.4.5 and the closural line at Song.4.7, with the 4:5|4:6 rival cut neither disclosed nor tested. CORRECTION to OL's framing: the BOUND itself stands - the closural form כֻּלָּ֤ךְ יָפָה֙ רַעְיָתִ֔י (byte, oshb:Song.4.7) is unique book-wide (sweep: 1 verse, skeleton tier) and the wasf-zone architecture names this zone with that closure, so no boundary change is proposed; the defect is the undisclosed interior refrain and the untested rival, which is exactly the rival-cut disclosure the Song.5.8 row in this cluster does perform. Limb 3 UPHELD and decisive: the form standing at oshb:Song.4.8 is מִלְּבָנ֣וֹן (byte), a prefix conjugation, and no imperative of that root occurs in the verse - the label is imported from the rendering “Come with me from Lebanon, my bride, with me from Lebanon.” (web:Song.4.8). The book does carry a real 2fs imperative of that root, וּב֣וֹאִי (byte, oshb:Song.4.16), which is precisely what MT 4:8 does not have. With no morphology layer staged, a form label must stand on the pointed bytes plus both renderings, and these bytes do not supply it. The forward rival survives on its other prong: כַּלָּ֔ה (byte, oshb:Song.4.8) is the bride-epithet's first site (sweep: 6 verses, word-bound: MT 4:8-4:12, 5:1). The inclusio the row argues verifies independently - the his-word-for-her anchor stands byte at oshb:Song.4.1 and byte at oshb:Song.4.7 inside a 9-verse book-wide set.
rulings.remedy: Three edits, one row (P01-017). (1) boundary_rationale: give the opener's formula claim its object, digit and tier - hinnakh-yafah-rayati, sweep: 2 verses, skeleton tier (MT 1:15 and MT 4:1), with MT 1:15 standing at accent_stripped tier against this run and opening no unit - and rest the seam on the inclusio rather than on the opener's uniqueness; word-bind the digit with the his-word-for-her anchor so the 2ms form at MT 1:16 cannot enter it. (2) device_notes: disclose the interior refrain (byte at oshb:Song.4.6, byte at oshb:Song.2.17; sweep: 2 verses) and state why it does not cut - no tier-1 voice-shift marker stands at 4:5|4:6, and the unique closural form at Song.4.7 (sweep: 1 verse, skeleton tier) brackets the unit. (3) strongest_rejected_alternative: delete the form label 'imperative' for Song.4.8, quote the prefix-conjugation form spliced and tier-labeled, and rest the forward rival on the bride-epithet's first site (sweep: 6 verses, word-bound). TESTS THE CURE MUST PASS: (1) every recurrence claim carries object + digit + tier at write time, and a formula whose other site does no boundary work must say so; (2) the disclosure must name the 4:5|4:6 rival cut and defeat it on bytes, matching the rival-cut disclosure the Song.5.8 row performs; (3) with no morphology layer staged, no form label may survive that the pointed bytes plus both renderings do not supply - a rendering's English imperative is not the form.

rulings.challenge_claim: The span-wide 'no addressee or gender-marked interruption' is carried by absence over the unit's last two verses and ships without a digit-bearing sweep, and the garden catchword crossing the row's own back seam is undisclosed. (severity as filed: low)
rulings.grounds: Both limbs verify from bytes, but the severity as filed understates the second, which is a mandated disclosure rather than a wording matter - hence refine, not plain uphold. Limb 2 (the operative defect): the garden lexeme straddles this row's own back seam byte-true and undisclosed - מַעְיַ֣ן גַּנִּ֔ים (byte, oshb:Song.4.15) then הָפִ֥יחִי גַנִּ֖י (byte, oshb:Song.4.16) then בָּ֣אתִי לְגַנִּי֮ (byte, oshb:Song.5.1) - inside a word-bound gan-family set of 7 verses (skeleton tier: MT 4:12, 4:15, 4:16, 5:1, 6:2, 6:11, 8:13), with the row's own in-span anchor at גַּ֥ן נָע֖וּל (byte, oshb:Song.4.12). Standing campaign law is explicit that a byte-true device straddling the row's own seam argues continuity AGAINST the row unless disclosed, and this straddle runs across two consecutive rows' seams. OL's hazard discipline on the digit is also exact and independently re-verified: the contained-substring hits at MT 4:4 and at oshb:Song.7.3 = web:Song.7.2 are false hits and are correctly excluded by word-binding. Limb 1 UPHELD but re-characterized: the address chain is attested by vocative or 2fs suffix at MT 4:8, 4:9, 4:10, 4:11, 4:12 and at שְׁלָחַ֨יִךְ֙ (byte, oshb:Song.4.13), and MT 4:14 and MT 4:15 carry no 2fs suffix and no vocative at all (“a fountain of gardens, a well of living waters, flowing streams from Lebanon.” at web:Song.4.15 concurs) - so the row's own back seam rests on a missing marker. The precise defect is not a missing sweep digit as filed (the sentence does carry '(sweep: 6 verses book-wide)', which independently verifies word-bound at MT 4:8-4:12 and 5:1) but a digit attached to a DIFFERENT object than the universal it sits beside: continuity across unmarked verses is tier-2 corroboration under the moderate voice policy and can never carry a seam alone. The seam is rescuable as a seam-pair edit, since the following verse supplies a tier-1 anchor on its own bytes. The K/Q-bearing MT 4:9 is correctly touched with no K/Q claim, and the setumah at MT 4:11 is carried as interior tier-3 single-witness corroboration.
rulings.remedy: Two edits, one row (P01-018), plus one seam-pair note. (1) device_notes: disclose the cross-seam straddle - the gan-family chain from oshb:Song.4.15 to oshb:Song.4.16 to oshb:Song.5.1 (sweep: 7 verses, word-bound, skeleton tier) - and state that the POSSESSOR change, not the lexeme, carries the seam. (2) boundary_rationale: replace 'with no addressee or gender-marked interruption across the whole span' with the attested positive chain and its honest stop (vocative or 2fs address through oshb:Song.4.13, none at MT 4:14-4:15), labelling the remainder tier-2 continuity and pointing the back seam at the following verse's own tier-1 anchor. Treat this back seam and the following row's front seam as ONE edit. TESTS THE CURE MUST PASS: no byte-true device may straddle the row's own seam undisclosed; any gan digit must be word-bound so that the contained-substring forms at MT 4:4 and at oshb:Song.7.3 = web:Song.7.2 cannot enter it; and every digit must sit adjacent to the claim about the object it actually counts.

rulings.challenge_claim: The possessor-shift argument is byte-false as stated: no 1cs 'my garden' form occurs anywhere in MT 4:8-4:15, and the only one at this seam stands inside Song.4.16 itself, in the woman's own address to the winds.
rulings.grounds: Byte-false as stated, confirmed by an independent word-bound sweep. Every garden token in the preceding unit is unsuffixed or plural: גַּ֥ן נָע֖וּל (byte, oshb:Song.4.12) and מַעְיַ֣ן גַּנִּ֔ים (byte, oshb:Song.4.15); a word-bound gan-family sweep over MT 4:8-4:15 returns no 1cs-suffixed form at any tier. The first 1cs form in the book's flow stands inside this row's own verse - הָפִ֥יחִי גַנִּ֖י (byte, oshb:Song.4.16), the woman's imperative to the wind - and the next in the man's speech at בָּ֣אתִי לְגַנִּי֮ (byte, oshb:Song.5.1). Both witnesses concur: “My sister, my bride, is a locked up garden; a locked up spring, a sealed fountain.” (web:Song.4.12) and “Blow on my garden, that its spices may flow out.” (web:Song.4.16). The row's boundary_rationale therefore locates a form in Song.4.8-Song.4.15 that is not there, and carries that half of its voice-shift argument with no quoted form at all, which the engagement standard bars for a boundary-relevant Hebrew claim; strongest_rejected_alternative repeats the same male-voice premise, so the defect is duplicated in a second field. The seam itself survives and no boundary change is proposed: יָבֹ֤א דוֹדִי֙ לְגַנּ֔וֹ וְיֹאכַ֖ל (byte, oshb:Song.4.16) is the her-word-for-him anchor (dodi-exact: 24 verses; distinct from the 28-verse dod-family, from the defective 'your loves' form standing twice inside MT 4:10 in the man's mouth, and from the plural at oshb:Song.5.1), and the shift actually attested runs her 'my garden' to 'his garden' INSIDE this one verse - tier-1 in-verse formula anchor, which is stronger evidence than the cross-unit shift the row asserted. Severity holds at medium rather than high because the cure is a re-cut sentence over evidence already in the row's own verse.
rulings.remedy: Field boundary_rationale (P01-019): delete the parenthetical locating 'my garden' in Song.4.8-Song.4.15 and re-cut the shift to the one attested inside this verse - her spliced 1cs garden form against the 3ms garden form in the same verse, both tier-labeled byte at oshb:Song.4.16 - keeping the her-word-for-him anchor as the tier-1 driver and naming its object (dodi-exact, 24 verses) where any digit is carried. Mirror the identical correction into strongest_rejected_alternative, which repeats the male-voice premise. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS (the test that killed the original): a word-bound gan-family sweep restricted to MT 4:8-4:15 must return the form the sentence claims - it currently returns no 1cs-suffixed form at any tier - and every boundary-relevant Hebrew claim must ship a spliced, tier-labeled form at the ref it is claimed for.

rulings.challenge_claim: Attributing Song.5.1's garden-report clause to 'the man' crosses the 4:16|5:1 voice seam without quoting the gender-marked formula anchor that grounds it, even though that evidence sits in the same verse the row already cites.
rulings.grounds: Verified on the bytes and squarely within the moderate voice-attribution policy. The row rests the man-voice premise on בָּ֣אתִי לְגַנִּי֮ (byte, oshb:Song.5.1), a 1cs perfect that is not gender-marked and cannot by itself carry a voice attribution; the attested tier-1 anchor sits two words later in the same verse, אֲחֹתִ֣י כַלָּה֒ (byte, oshb:Song.5.1), his address vocabulary (bride-epithet form: 5 verses, word-bound, MT 4:9, 4:10, 4:12, 5:1, 5:2; kallah: 6 verses, MT 4:8-4:12 and 5:1), and is never quoted. The policy is explicit that every voice-shift seam claim quotes the gender-marked or attested-anchor Hebrew form, spliced and tier-labeled, and that continuity alone is tier-2 corroboration - so as shipped the cross-part seam is argued at tier-2 while tier-1 evidence lies unquoted inside the row's own span. LF's audit of the row against heading-leaning is correct and worth recording: the tier-4 speaker apparatus is explicitly refused and the plural-summons hedge is held open at the tier the bytes support, so the defect is a missing quotation, not a heading-lean. CONVERGENCE: this row is also challenged by OL. The two items are DISTINCT defects - LF's is the missing in-verse tier-1 anchor for the man-voice premise; OL's is the unanchored cross-part continuity assertion plus two undisclosed byte-true straddles - but they share one root, recorded here as a NEW FINDING neither primary states: the 4:16|5:1 seam is argued from its own bytes by NEITHER row. P01-019 defers the boundary forward ('that reply belongs to the verse immediately following it, argued separately on its own bytes') and P02-001 defers it backward ('closing the movement that opened before this part's own span'), so a seam that IS byte-supportable at tier-1 from both sides - her-word-for-him at oshb:Song.4.16 against his address vocabulary at oshb:Song.5.1 - currently has no tier-1 driver stated in either row. The launch note is right that this is a work-unit boundary and not a literary claim; the mutual deferral is the hazard that boundary created.
rulings.remedy: Field boundary_rationale (P02-001), executed as ONE seam-pair edit with P01-019: quote the tier-1 anchor already standing in the verse - his address vocabulary at oshb:Song.5.1, spliced and tier-labeled byte, with its object named (bride-epithet form: 5 verses; kallah: 6 verses, both word-bound) - as the ground for the man's voice, instead of resting it on a 1cs perfect. State the seam positively from both sides so neither row defers it to the other. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS (the test that killed the original): the voice attribution must be carried by a quoted, spliced, tier-labeled gender-marked or attested-anchor form; a 1cs perfect carries no gender and cannot pass, and the cure must not migrate to the tier-4 speaker apparatus, which remains never-evidence in either direction.

rulings.challenge_claim: The cross-part continuity the row asserts is left with no byte anchor while two byte-true chains straddle its front seam undisclosed, and the widened-address point leans on the WEB rendering of a dod-family plural the row never names. (severity as filed: low)
rulings.grounds: Limbs 1 and 2 verify; limb 3 is largely conceded by OL itself and should not carry weight; severity as filed is too low, because the undisclosed straddles are a mandated disclosure that argues continuity against this row's own front seam at the cross-part boundary - hence refine. Limb 1 UPHELD: the rationale asserts that the verse closes a movement opened before the part's own span while naming no verse and quoting no form, and the front-seam neighbour appears nowhere in boundary_evidence_refs. Limb 2 UPHELD and re-derived: two byte-true chains straddle the front seam undisclosed - יָבֹ֤א דוֹדִי֙ לְגַנּ֔וֹ וְיֹאכַ֖ל (byte, oshb:Song.4.16) answered clause-for-clause by בָּ֣אתִי לְגַנִּי֮ with its eat-verb echo at אָכַ֤לְתִּי (both byte, oshb:Song.5.1), and אֲחֹתִ֣י כַלָּה֒ (byte, oshb:Song.5.1) continuing the man's address vocabulary attested at MT 4:9, 4:10 and 4:12 (bride-epithet form: 5 verses; kallah: 6 verses, word-bound). Standing law makes an undisclosed byte-true cross-seam device an argument for continuity against the row, and here it bears directly on whether Song.5.1 should be held with Song.4.16 at all. Limb 3 REFINED DOWN: the widened-address claim is in fact byte-anchored independently of any rendering by אִכְל֣וּ רֵעִ֔ים (byte, oshb:Song.5.1), which OL concedes; what genuinely remains is that the verse-final דּוֹדִֽים (byte, oshb:Song.5.1) is a dod-family plural, a different object from the 24-verse dodi-exact set of the surrounding verses and the form the closing word of “Eat, friends! Drink, yes, drink abundantly, beloved.” (web:Song.5.1) renders - unnamed where the rendering is cited. That is a naming gap, not a leaning defect. CONVERGENCE: distinct from LF's item on this row (missing in-verse tier-1 anchor), with the shared root recorded in that ruling - the 4:16|5:1 seam is argued by neither row on its own bytes. The setumah at MT 5:1 is correctly tiered single-witness and the tier-4 speaker apparatus is explicitly refused.
rulings.remedy: Two edits, one row (P02-001), merged with the P02-001/LF edit as one seam-pair cure. (1) boundary_evidence_refs: add the front-seam neighbour (web:Song.4.16 and oshb:Song.4.16), which the continuity assertion argues but does not mirror. (2) device_notes: disclose both straddles - the garden-and-eat answer from oshb:Song.4.16 to oshb:Song.5.1, and the address-vocabulary chain continuing from oshb:Song.4.12 - and state why the possessor change and the addressee change still cut the seam; where the rendering's closing 'beloved' is cited, name the verse-final form as a dod-family plural, distinct from the 24-verse dodi-exact object. TESTS THE CURE MUST PASS: every verse argued in prose outside the row's own span must appear in boundary_evidence_refs; no byte-true device may straddle the row's own seam undisclosed; and the widened-address claim must rest on the spliced plural summons at oshb:Song.5.1, not on the rendering.

rulings.challenge_claim: Both of the row's seams carry undisclosed byte-true straddles - the man's address vocabulary continues into MT 5:2 and the daughters quote the oath back at MT 5:9 - while the opening voice claim is carried by the English rather than by the gender-marked Hebrew.
rulings.grounds: All three limbs verify on re-derived bytes. Front seam: פִּתְחִי לִ֞י אֲחֹתִ֤י רַעְיָתִי֙ (byte, oshb:Song.5.2) continues the man's address vocabulary across the seam - the bride-epithet chain of MT 4:9, 4:10, 4:12 and 5:1 (5 verses, word-bound) plus his-word-for-her (9 verses book-wide) - and the qol-dodi opener stands in the same verse (2 sites book-wide). The role split that resolves it is available in both witnesses and is neither performed nor disclosed: the rendering marks the address as embedded direct speech inside her narration (“It is the voice of my beloved who knocks” introducing the quoted call at web:Song.5.2), which is what distinguishes continued address from quoted address - exactly the same speech-role discipline this row already applies elsewhere. Opening voice: the form that actually marks it, אֲנִ֥י יְשֵׁנָ֖ה (byte, oshb:Song.5.2, feminine singular), is never quoted, and the claim rests on “I was asleep, but my heart was awake.” (web:Song.5.2), which carries no gender at all, plus a tier-3 setumah at MT 5:1 - so a tier-1 marker present in the row's own opening verse goes unused while the seam is argued below its available tier. Back seam: שֶׁכָּ֖כָה (byte, oshb:Song.5.9) repeats the oath root immediately across the row's own closing seam, the daughters quoting it back - undisclosed, and it is precisely the same-root site the four-site adjuration count excludes on speech-role grounds (oath root: 5 verses; adjuration sites: 4), so the row's own shape discipline owed the disclosure. That discipline is otherwise exact and no boundary change is proposed: both adjuration quotes collate byte at oshb:Song.5.8 and the shape is correctly held apart from the full daughters-plus-gazelles form and from the third variant, with no harmonized shape anywhere, and the rival of isolating the refrain verse is explicitly disclosed - the one refrain-verse decision in this cluster that discharges that duty.
rulings.remedy: Two fields, one row (P02-002). (1) boundary_rationale: quote the feminine-marked opening form at oshb:Song.5.2, spliced and tier-labeled byte, as the ground for the opening voice, keeping the rendering as corroboration only. (2) device_notes: disclose both straddles and perform the speech-role split - the address vocabulary continuing into MT 5:2 stands INSIDE the man's quoted call framed by her narration, not as continued address across the seam; and the oath root recurring at MT 5:9 is the daughters quoting it back, the same-root site the four-site count excludes on speech-role grounds.
